key_insight: Stoichiometry-preserved ionic clusters plus pretrained MLIPs can predict detonation performance of multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are known.
engineering_relevance: This offers a synthesis-facing screening tool for data-scarce materials discovery, reducing reliance on expensive crystal-structure prediction and experimental trial-and-error.
method: Represent each candidate as a non-periodic stoichiometric ionic-cluster formula unit.
Fine-tune a pretrained atomistic MLIP with a multi-task energy–force objective to regularize sparse property labels.
Use the surrogate to screen candidate PEMs and generalize to unseen stoichiometries and cation chemistries.
evidence_signal: On 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials, the method achieved cross-validated screening and later matched three new ABX4 materials with a mean absolute error of 92 m·s^-1 versus Kamlet–Jacobs detonation velocities.
watch_item: Performance depends on a small, carefully curated dataset, so out-of-distribution chemistry or poorly represented ionic packings may reduce reliability.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
